unit.why: A short anecdote reported by the tzaddik (R. Moshe Leib of Sasov): he overheard drunken villagers talking and learned from them what love of Israel means. It has a minimal event and a moral lesson.

stories.start_quote: אמר הה״ק ז"לז״כ שלמד אהבת ישראל מכפרי
stories.end_quote: ולסבול כל מכאובם. ובצרתם לו צר
stories.summary_en: The tzaddik says he learned love of Israel from a drunken villager. The villager asked his friend whether he loved him, then rebuked him: a true friend would know what he lacked. The tzaddik concluded that loving Israel means feeling every lack and pain of one's fellow Jews.

quotes: כי אהבת ישראל הוא להרגיש כל מחסורם
tags.why: The point is the virtue of love of Israel.
Framed as moral instruction ('from this he learned') in love of one's fellow.
The exchange takes place over wine at a drinking party.

quotes: מכפרי אחד שהי׳ במסובה עם כפריים אחרים
tags.why: The villagers are probably gentile peasants, as in other versions of this tale.
Told by the tzaddik as an exemplum with a moral, close to a mashal.

quotes: כי אהבת ישראל הוא להרגיש כל מחסורם ולסבול כל מכאובם
tags.why: Ends with the tzaddik's teaching drawn from the anecdote.

missing_concepts: learning a religious lesson from simple or gentile folk
